main_body: Red barn: a large tiled roof slope with a dormer, above a vertical-plank wall with a big double door, two small windows and a stone base
top_band: Roof slope in red-orange tiles from row 5 to row 57, with a cream ridge highlight at rows 5-8 and a cream eave edge line at rows 56-57; it reads as a surface seen from above
evidence: Reading down the middle column: the ridge cap, then the tile slope (rows 9-55), then a cream eave line (rows 56-57), then a dark eave shadow (rows 58-60), then the plank wall and door down to a stone base at rows 89-93. The roof is a large shaded slope, not a thin rim. The dormer sits on the slope and the door and windows have dark inset frames. This matches how the reference roofs read as top surfaces above their walls.

style.evidence: The roof tiles have 4-5 tones and a regular scallop pattern, but it is a repeated stamp with no per-tile variation and no clumping. The wall is only 3-4 tones of vertical stripes. The door bracing and window frames are flat light-grey lines on red. The stone base is a flat grey band with little shading, unlike the reference stones shaded one by one. A thick near-black outline runs around the whole roof, door and building, which gives a sticker look beside the reference's tinted, selective outlines. Overall it is flatter and more uniform than the references.
